questions.question: Sampark Kranti Express left Delhi for Chennai at 14:30 hours, travelling at a speed of 75 km/h, while Rajdhani Express left Delhi for Chennai on the same day at 16:30 hours, travelling at a speed of 90 km/h, travelling on the same route. How far away from Delhi will the two trains meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for meeting distance: D = [S₁ × S₂ × Time Difference] ÷ (S₂ − S₁)

Here, S₁ = 75 km/h, S₂ = 90 km/h, and Time Difference = 16:30 − 14:30 = 2 hours.

D = [75 × 90 × 2] ÷ (90 − 75)

D = 13500 ÷ 15

D = 900 km

**∴ The correct answer is 900 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Sampark Kranti Express = 75 km/h

Departure time of Sampark Kranti = 14:30 hours

Speed of Rajdhani Express = 90 km/h

Departure time of Rajdhani = 16:30 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/533cac8a0b372a20361cb141dc94fe403fdc0c1e9219afb3626028e48260bb13.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time difference between the departures = 16:30 − 14:30 = 2 hours.

⇒ Distance covered by Sampark Kranti Express in these 2 hours = 75 × 2 = 150 km.

⇒ This 150 km is the head start distance between the two trains.

⇒ Relative speed of Rajdhani Express with respect to Sampark Kranti = 90 − 75 = 15 km/h.

⇒ Time taken by Rajdhani Express to catch up = Distance ÷ Relative speed.

⇒ Catch up time = 150 ÷ 15 = 10 hours.

⇒ The meeting distance from Delhi = Speed of Rajdhani × Time taken.

⇒ Distance = 90 × 10 = 900 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 900 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂). When they move in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Catch-up Time Formula

Time to meet = Head start distance ÷ Relative speed. This determines the duration required for the faster object to overtake the slower one.

Average Speed

When a journey covers two equal halves at different speeds S₁ and S₂, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

questions.question: A man covers a certain distance at a speed of 75 km/h in 8 hours. To cover the same distance in 6 hours, his speed needs to be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance covered in 8 hours at a speed of 75 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Distance = 75 km/h × 8 hours

Distance = 600 km

To cover the same distance in 6 hours, his speed needs to be:

Let the required speed be x km/h.

Distance = Speed × Time

600 km = x km/h × 6 hours

⇒ x = 600 km / 6 hours

⇒ x = 100 km/h

**The required speed to cover the same distance in 6 hours is 100 km/h.**

The diagram below shows a section of phloem tissue in plants. Which labelling shows the part with perforated walls that helps in transportation?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aae19f24d195d362167fd07127115cbbe22814a3e116d75499397862931bf3b4.png]
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The part labeled 'b' in the phloem tissue is known as the sieve tube element.
 
• Sieve tube elements are characterized by their perforated walls, known as sieve plates, which facilitate the transport of nutrients.
 
• The main function of sieve tube elements is to** transport organic substances**, such as sugars, throughout the plant.
 
• Sieve plates are crucial for maintaining the flow of phloem sap between adjacent sieve tube elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phloem Tissue:**

 
 
• Phloem is one of the two types of **vascular tissue **in plants, the other being xylem.
 
• It is responsible for the transport of organic nutrients, particularly sucrose, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
 
 
• **Sieve Tube Elements:**
 
 
• Sieve tube elements are specialized cells that form **long tubes for the transportation of phloem sap**.
 
• They lack a nucleus and have fewer organelles to facilitate the easy flow of sap.
 
 
 
• **Sieve Plates:**
 
 
• Sieve plates are the end walls of sieve tube elements that are perforated to** allow the flow of sap between cells**.
 
• They play a critical role in maintaining the continuity of the phloem transport system.
 
 
 
• **Companion Cells:**
 
 
• Companion cells are closely associated with sieve tube elements and aid in their function.
 
• They provide metabolic support and help in the loading and unloading of sugars into the sieve tubes.

questions.question: A solid metallic sphere of radius 12 cm is melted and recast into 27 identical spheres. What is the ratio of the surface area of the original sphere to the total surface area of 6 smaller spheres so formed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the original sphere = 12 cm

The large sphere is melted and recast into 27 identical smaller spheres.

**Formula used:**

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr³

Surface area of a sphere = 4πr²

**Step 1: Find the radius of the smaller spheres**

Let the radius of each smaller sphere be r.

Volume of the original sphere = Volume of 27 smaller spheres

⇒ (4/3)π(12)³ = 27 × (4/3)πr³

Cancel out common terms:

⇒ 12³ = 27 × r³

⇒ 1728 = 27 × r³

⇒ r³ = 1728 / 27

⇒ r³ = 64

⇒ r = 4 cm

**Step 2: Calculate the surface area**

Surface area of the original sphere = 4π(12)² = 4π(144) = 576π cm²

Surface area of one smaller sphere = 4π(4)² = 4π(16) = 64π cm²

Total surface area of 6 smaller spheres = 6 × 64π = 384π cm²

**Step 3: Find the ratio of surface areas**

Ratio = Surface area of original sphere / Surface area of 6 smaller spheres

⇒ Ratio = 576π / 384π

⇒ Ratio = 576 / 384 = 3 / 2

**∴ The ratio of the surface area of the original sphere to the total surface area of 6 smaller spheres is 3:2.**

questions.question: Let x be the greatest number which, when divides 7072, 8505 and 9925, the remainders are 22, 45 and 55, respectively. What is the sum of the digits of x?

**Formula Used:**

The greatest number x that leaves specific remainders when dividing given numbers can be found using the formula:

Given numbers: 7072, 8505, 9925

Remainders: 22, 45, 55

Calculate the differences:

7050 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 5 × 47

8460 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 × 47

9870 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 7 × 47

questions.question: A shopkeeper offers the following schemes on toys of the same marked price. (A) Successive discounts of 12% and 15% on any number of toys bought. (B) Successive discounts of 15%, 10% and 2% on any number of toys bought. (C) 40% discount on the first 3 toys and 15% discount on each toy thereon. (D) 2 toys free of cost on buying 10 toys. A customer wants to buy 10 toys. Which of the above schemes is most beneficial to her?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price of each toy = M

Number of toys to be bought = 10

**Formula Used:**

For successive discounts: Final price = Marked price × (1 - d₁) × (1 - d₂) × ... × (1 - dₙ)

For free toys: Total toys received = Toys bought + Free toys

**Calculation:**

**Scheme (A):**

Successive discounts of 12% and 15%

Discounted price = M × (1 - 0.12) × (1 - 0.15)

⇒ Discounted price = M × 0.88 × 0.85

⇒ Discounted price = 0.748M

Total cost for 10 toys = 10 × 0.748M

⇒ Total cost = 7.48M

**Scheme (B):**

Successive discounts of 15%, 10%, and 2%

Discounted price = M × (1 - 0.15) × (1 - 0.10) × (1 - 0.02)

⇒ Discounted price = M × 0.85 × 0.90 × 0.98

⇒ Discounted price = 0.7506M

Total cost for 10 toys = 10 × 0.7506M

⇒ Total cost = 7.506M

**Scheme (C):**

40% discount on the first 3 toys and 15% discount on each toy thereafter

Cost of first 3 toys = 3 × M × (1 - 0.40)

⇒ Cost of first 3 toys = 3 × 0.60M

⇒ Cost of first 3 toys = 1.8M

Cost of remaining 7 toys = 7 × M × (1 - 0.15)

⇒ Cost of remaining 7 toys = 7 × 0.85M

⇒ Cost of remaining 7 toys = 5.95M

Total cost for 10 toys = 1.8M + 5.95M

⇒ Total cost = 7.75M

**Scheme (D):**

2 toys free on buying 10 toys

Total toys received = 10 + 2 = 12

Cost for 10 toys = 10 × M

Cost per toy = 10M / 12

⇒ Cost per toy = 0.8333M

Total cost for 10 toys = 10 × 0.8333M

⇒ Total cost = 8.333M

**Comparison:**

Scheme (A): 7.48M

Scheme (B): 7.506M

Scheme (C): 7.75M

Scheme (D): 8.333M

**The most beneficial scheme is (A) with a total cost of 7.48M.**

**Given:**

The ratio of incomes of Seema and Darshan is 7 ∶ 5.

Seema saves ₹12,000 and Darshan saves ₹9,000.

The ratio of their expenditures is 17 ∶ 12.

**Formula Used:**

Total expenditure = Expenditure of Seema + Expenditure of Darshan

**Calculation:**

Let the incomes of Seema and Darshan be 7x and 5x, respectively.

Savings of Seema = Income of Seema - Expenditure of Seema

⇒ 12,000 = 7x - Expenditure of Seema

⇒ Expenditure of Seema = 7x - 12,000

Savings of Darshan = Income of Darshan - Expenditure of Darshan

⇒ 9,000 = 5x - Expenditure of Darshan

⇒ Expenditure of Darshan = 5x - 9,000

Given, the ratio of their expenditures is 17 ∶ 12.

⇒ (7x - 12,000) / (5x - 9,000) = 17 / 12

Cross-multiplying,

⇒ 12(7x - 12,000) = 17(5x - 9,000)

⇒ 84x - 144,000 = 85x - 153,000

⇒ 85x - 84x = 153,000 - 144,000

⇒ x = 9,000

Income of Seema = 7x = 7 × 9,000 = 63,000

Income of Darshan = 5x = 5 × 9,000 = 45,000

Expenditure of Seema = 7x - 12,000 = 63,000 - 12,000 = 51,000

Expenditure of Darshan = 5x - 9,000 = 45,000 - 9,000 = 36,000

Total expenditure = Expenditure of Seema + Expenditure of Darshan

⇒ Total expenditure = 51,000 + 36,000 = 87,000

**The total expenditure of Seema and Darshan is ₹87,000.**

__
 
• A solenoid produces a **uniform magnetic field** inside it.
 
• This means that the magnetic field strength is the same at all points within the solenoid, regardless of the distance from the centre.
 
• This uniformity is due to the way the magnetic field lines are arranged within the solenoid.
 
• The field lines are parallel to each other and run the length of the solenoid.
 
• This creates a consistent magnetic field throughout the interior space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The magnetic field inside a long solenoid is uniform for several reasons related to the structure and operation of the solenoid:
 
• Even Distribution of Turns: In a solenoid, the wire is wound evenly around a cylindrical form, creating a series of loops or turns that are distributed along the length of the solenoid. This even distribution of turns ensures that, at every point inside the solenoid (except near the ends), there is an equal contribution to the magnetic field from each coil of wire.
 
• Parallel Magnetic Field Lines: Due to the shape and arrangement of the coils, the magnetic field lines inside the solenoid are nearly parallel to each other and to the longitudinal axis of the solenoid. This parallelism results from the superposition of the magnetic fields produced by each turn of the solenoid, with the directional components perpendicular to the axis canceling out and only the components along the axis adding up. This creates a uniform direction and magnitude of the magnetic field in the central region of the solenoid.
 
• Negligible Edge Effects: In a long solenoid, the effects that disrupt uniformity, such as the fringing of the magnetic field, are significant only near the ends of the solenoid. In the central region, these effects are negligible, contributing to the uniformity of the magnetic field.

__
 
• P.K. Thungon Committee got constitutional recognition for the local government bodies.
 
• PK Thungan Committee is related to Panchayati raj.
 
• In 1989 the P.K. Thungon Committee recommended constitutional recognition for the local government bodies.

__
 
• Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957): The committee submitted its report in November 1957, in which the term ‘democratic decentralization‘ first appears. The important recommendations are:

 
 
• Transfer of resources and power to these bodies to be ensured.
 
• District Collector to be the chairman of Zila Parishad.
 
• ​Establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system – gram panchayat at village level (direct election), Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and Zila Parishad at the district level (indirect election).
 
• Rajasthan (1959) adopted the system first, followed by Andhra Pradesh in the same year.

• A minister for Panchayati Raj to be appointed by the state council of ministers.
 
• Zila Parishad to be made responsible for planning at the state level.
 
• Compulsory powers of taxation to be given to these institutions.
 
• Political parties should participate at all levels in the elections.
 
• The three-tier system is to be replaced by a two-tier system.
 
 
 
• G V K Rao Committee (1985): ​The important recommendations of the G V K Rao Committee are:
 
 
• Regular elections to be held.
 
• Post of DDC (District Development Commissioner) to be created acting as the chief executive officer of the Zila Parishad.
 
• ​Zila Parishad to be given prime importance and all developmental programs at that level to be handed to it.
 
 
 
• L M Singhvi Committee (1986): The committee was constituted by the Rajiv Gandhi government on ‘Revitalisation of Panchayati Raj institutions for Democracy and Development. ​​The important recommendations are:
 
 
• Nyaya Panchayats to be established for clusters of villages.
 
• Constitutional recognition for Panchayati Raj institution

• PRI was constitutionalized through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 to build democracy at the grassroots level and was entrusted with the task of rural development in the country.

• This stiff competition negatively impacted Indian handicraft industries, which struggled to compete with the efficiency and affordability of machine-made goods.
 
• As British industries flooded the market with cheaper and more uniform products, the demand for traditional Indian handicrafts significantly declined.
 
• Consumers began to favour the mass-produced items due to their lower prices and perceived quality, leading to reduced sales for local artisans and craftsmen.

• Many traditional crafts used locally sourced materials, which were not the limiting factor.
